header_summary:
The Bitcoin Development Mailing List highlighted the necessity of a foundational Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) system for the effective implementation of the commit/reveal mechanism in Bitcoin, emphasizing that without such a system, the strategy is unsuitable for systems that delay updates ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/CAHPaHkr5r4+hodZv6F2S1yCq_UcHSr2iCrkYLgZ_vryNgwbRPA@mail.gmail.com/T/#mfa1857336e77db8f1b71e94d042094ffbaa2226a)). 

Michael, known as fanquake, released new test binaries for Bitcoin, enhancing compatibility and security across various architectures, and highlighted the community’s role in improving the software’s reliability through feedback and bug reporting ([source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/391ad3ce-2352-42d8-9d15-e011e187cb0fn@googlegroups.com/T/#m5ddf81712d352faf60e6e636157f336e53b5b434)). 

In the Rust programming environment, the development of `seedroller` and `keyderiver` tools was discussed, which improve the security and reliability of cryptographic operations. These tools are designed to generate and derive cryptographic keys with minimal external dependencies, and the community is encouraged to contribute to their development ([bitcoin-key-tools](https://github.com/bubb1es71/bitcoin-key-tools)). 

Another cryptographic strategy ensures encrypted outputs are uniformly 108 characters long, using rejection sampling to maintain consistency and enhance security, with potential future improvements including a checksum for additional security verification ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/pq-single-address-backup-bip-38-for-p2mr-bc1z-104-char-encrypted-backup-format/2767/7)).

recent_posts.title: DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol
recent_posts.summary: - The commit/reveal mechanism depends on a valid Post-Quantum Cryptography UTXO.  - It is not a starting solution for systems delaying Bitcoin updates.  - Effective implementation requires prior establishment of a robust PQC system.

recent_posts.title: static-pie release binaries available for testing
recent_posts.summary:
- Michael released new Bitcoin test binaries with updated glibc version 2.44.
- Binaries for multiple architectures ensure compatibility and include security hashes.
- Community feedback is crucial to the ongoing enhancement of Bitcoin software.

recent_posts.title: Seedroller and keyderiver: cli tools to generate BIP39 seed words and derive BIP380 keys
recent_posts.summary: - The `seedroller` tool generates BIP39 seeds using dice and system entropy.  - `keyderiver` derives BIP380 key expressions from BIP39 seeds.  - Both tools, available on GitHub, seek community feedback for improvements.

recent_posts.title: PQ-single-address-backup - BIP-38 for P2MR (bc1z) - 104-char encrypted backup format
recent_posts.summary:
- The strategy ensures 108-character encrypted outputs using rejection sampling for efficient encoding.
- A uniform 108-character length simplifies verification and enhances security by identifying transcription errors.
- Future plans include integrating a checksum in a shared header to augment security and interoperability.

recent_posts.title: Boomerang: Bitcoin Cold Storage with Built-In Coercion Resistance
recent_posts.summary:
- The email details redundancy improvements for "Boomlet" and other system components.
- Backup activation for the Boomlet is undeveloped, signaling a need for future work.
- Incorporation of a recovery checklist aims to enhance disaster management efficiency.

active_posts.title: Giving teeth to expected EC disabling: P2XX(-T)(-ML)
active_posts.summary: - Bitcoin devs explore disabling EC opcodes to address quantum threats.  - Two proposals, Tripwire and Miner Lockdown, aim for rapid, user-driven responses.  - Integrating these rules directly supports timely, decentralized security enhancements.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Anti-Fee-Sniping with LockTime
active_posts.summary:
- The new BIP326 is formalizing an anti-fee-sniping feature using nSequence for taproot transactions.
- It sets nLockTime to the blockchain tip height, with specific conditions for stabilization.
- Test vectors in the BIP draft help developers understand and implement these changes effectively.

active_posts.title: post-quantum: solution ideas to "tripwire"game-theory issues + a certificate-based rescue protocol
active_posts.summary: - Mitigating game-theory risks in blockchain with quantum computing involves complex solutions.  - Strategies include leveraging NUMS and group signatures for enhanced security measures.  - Technical solutions also focus on using Bitcoin blockchain for secure timestamped certificates.

active_posts.title: Segwit commitment to post-quantum witness data?
active_posts.summary:
- Enhancing blockchain for post-quantum cryptography includes increasing block sizes for new data areas.
- Implementing these changes requires significant updates to mining and P2P network infrastructures.
- Alternative solutions could integrate post-quantum data within existing frameworks to minimize disruptions.

active_posts.title: Running Core's real consensus code inside a zkVM
active_posts.summary:
- Hazync system preserves Bitcoin Core logic, generating valid block STARK proofs without core rule reimplementation.
- It enables verification through past validated proofs, reducing computational demands while maintaining security.
- Hazync facilitates community participation in proof generation and allows independent proof verification via a browser tool.

active_posts.title: PQC output type discussion
active_posts.summary: - The email discusses strategies to protect Bitcoin from quantum threats using PQC and ECC.  - It introduces a P2TRv2 output type for immediate quantum threat mitigation and ease of adoption.  - A long-term strategy involves transitioning to a P2MR-based output for post-quantum resilience.

today_in_history_posts.title: Combined CTV+APO to minimal TXHASH+CSFS
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- The proposal integrates aspects of bip118 and bip119, aiming to resolve their limitations.
- It introduces three new Tapscript opcodes for enhanced transaction scripting and safety.
- Discussion seeks feedback on efficiency impacts, compatibility features, and signature specifications.

today_in_history_posts.title: Disclosure: Fake channel DoS vector
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- A DoS vector affecting all node implementations was discovered last year.
- Recent node software updates include defenses against this DoS attack.
- Users should upgrade to specific versions to protect their funds.

today_in_history_posts.title: Eclipsing Bitcoin Nodes with BGP Interception Attacks
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- A stealthier variant of BGP hijacking threatens the Bitcoin network with eclipse attacks.
- Attackers control Bitcoin traffic by manipulating BGP routes, enabling abuse like double spending.
- Proposed mitigations include using networking data for defense and traceroute for route-aware peer selection.
